wind.note: time coordinate is 'valid_time' in this file, not 'time' as in ow-0009's wind.nc -- auto-detected by fwd.forcing._detect_wind_time_dim

physics.formula: u_oil = current_drift_factor*uo + wind_drift_factor*u10; v_oil = current_drift_factor*vo + wind_drift_factor*v10

nan_coastline_policy.fallback: 3x3 then 5x5 inverse-distance-weighted valid-ocean neighbors, minimum 4 valid neighbors, weight=1/(d^2+epsilon)

known_limitations: Hotspot alert logic uses a >=30% minimum-fraction-of-active-particles rule (per zone), the same user-directed rule now in effect for ow-0009 (see progress.md's post-F07 revision 3) -- a deliberate, documented deviation from README section 10's originally locked 'any single particle triggers the zone' rule.

This case starts only ~29 km from the nearest CMEMS-masked land cell (vs ~77 km for ow-0009) and Beirut Port is CRITICAL from t0 through the final hour -- a genuinely different regime from ow-0009's always-offshore case.

Spherical-Earth displacement approximation (iste.geometry.metres_to_degrees) vs OpenDrift's WGS84-ellipsoidal pyproj.Geod remains a known source of small residual error in the OpenOil comparison (see the printed investigation and progress.md).
ERA5 wind file for this case uses 'valid_time' as its time coordinate name (not 'time' as in ow-0009's file) -- handled by auto-detection in fwd.forcing, not a hard-coded fix.

Land classification source is the static CMEMS uo/vo NaN mask, not an independent coastline shapefile (none exists in this project's environment); OpenDrift's reference run uses its own real GSHHG coastline instead, a genuine methodological difference documented in this case's own comparison script/output.
No frontend/application exists anywhere in this workspace to consume these outputs; outputs are standalone files for now.
